name: Illinois
agency: Illinois Secretary of State, Driver Services Department
permitAge: 15 (ages 15-17 with proof of enrollment in an approved driver education course; from 17 years 3 months without driver education). Must pass vision and written tests (handbook p. 16).

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, with a parent, legal guardian or licensed adult 21 or older with at least one year of driving experience (handbook p. 16, 18)
teen.holdPermit: At least 9 consecutive months (ages 15-17); permit valid 24 months. A moving violation conviction during the permit phase means a new 9-month wait (handbook p. 16, 18; ILSOS GDL page)
teen.nightLimit: Permit and initial license phases, under 18: Sunday to Thursday 10 p.m. to 6 a.m., Friday and Saturday 11 p.m. to 6 a.m.; local curfews may differ (handbook p. 18). Exemptions include driving to or from work or school activities (Parent-Teen Driving Guide)
teen.passengerLimit: First 12 months of license or until 18, whichever comes first: one passenger under 20, not counting siblings, stepsiblings, children or stepchildren. Permit phase: one in front, back seat limited to the number of belts (handbook p. 18)
teen.phone: Under 19: no phone use at all, hands-free included, except an emergency call to police, health care or emergency services (handbook p. 18-19). All drivers: no hand-held phone or texting; hands-free allowed from 19 (handbook p. 22).

bac.under21: any trace of alcohol (zero tolerance: above 0.00 and under 0.08, handbook p. 52, 60); suspension at least 3 months

notes: Handbook: Illinois Rules of the Road 2026, DSD A 112.47, printed July 2026 (PDF created 2026-07-13). Read in full on 2026-10-09. Printed page = PDF page minus 3. The old URL /publications/pdf_publications/dsd_a112.pdf redirects to /content/dam/publications/pdf_publications/dsd_a112.pdf.
Spanish edition: Manual de conducir en Illinois 2026, dsd_a113.pdf on ilsos.gov.
Three attempts per exam within one year of paying the fee (handbook p. 13).
Speed limits unless posted (handbook p. 24): interstates and tollways 70, four-lane highways 65, other highways and rural 55, city/town 30, alleys 15, school zones 20.

School bus: stop at least 20 feet before it (Illinois State Police press release, Aug. 11, 2025; not in handbook). Handbook p. 32: no stop needed only when both are on a four-lane road and the bus faces the other way.
Move over (Scott's Law): handbook p. 25 (stationary emergency/maintenance vehicles) and p. 45 (disabled vehicle with hazard lights on a four-lane highway).
ISP press release (Aug. 2025) gives school zone hours as 7 a.m. to 4 p.m.; the 2026 handbook p. 24-25 says 6:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.

Test format (92 Ill. Adm. Code 1030.80(b), amended effective July 1, 2026): the Class D written test has at least 35 questions and 80 percent must be correct (28 of 35). Not stated in the handbook (p. 14 says multiple-choice and true-or-false).

Test languages (92 Ill. Adm. Code 1030.80(d)-(f)): the written test is in English and may be in other languages the Secretary of State finds necessary from demand; oral test for illiterate applicants; an interpreter may be used (not for CDL tests). Handbook p. 15: oral exams on request Monday to Thursday. Which languages are offered was not confirmed.
